column1: # Curated per-deposition notes. Hand-written and git-tracked.
# The first detector flags any (deposition, nucleus) channel lying entirely outside the
# range that nucleus occupies across the whole corpus.
# Every row below was then checked against the BMRB archive itself via api.bmrb.io, so
# `verified` means "the deposited record was read", not "the scan fired".
#   recoverable  the correct values are present in the archive under another tag
#   defect       the values are physically impossible for that nucleus, cause identified
#   suspect      out of range, cause not established -- do not act on without checking
# recovery:    how to recover, or "-" if there is nothing to recover
# 2026-09-27: a second detector. The scan above is a RANGE scan and by construction cannot
# see a channel whose values are all physically plausible and only ORDERED wrongly. Those
# are found instead by correlating a deposited series against predictions from independent
# predictors (ProCS15, SPARTA+, UCBShift-X, SHIFTX2; DeepShift is not one of
# them) is negative -- and are listed in benchmarks/reference/anticorrelated_channels.json with the
# archive read-back that confirms each one. UCBShift found the same class of defect in
# their own test set (Chem. Sci. 2020, 11, 3180, Methods and ESI Fig. S1).
#   status anticorrelated  every independent predictor disagrees in sign with the deposited series

Val and Val_err are transposed in the archive: every H is deposited as 0.02 and every N as 0.20 ppm -- the canonical uncertainties -- while the real shifts sit in Val_err (H 7.36-9.98 ppm, 53 distinct; N 107.40-126.30, 49 distinct). Atom_type is correct. Fully recoverable by swapping the two tags. This is the ONLY deposition in the corpus with this failure, and its H cells reach the training labels.

HD2 rows carry 23.5-67.8 ppm with Atom_type=H -- carbon-magnitude values under a proton atom name. No Val_err to recover from. One of six sibling entries (505, 812, 813, 814, 1486, 1487) with the identical pattern, all early single- to four-digit depositions.

CG2 at 48.3-54.7 ppm (corpus 13.1-25.8) and CE1 at 32.5-54.7 (corpus 113.3-141.7), both Atom_type=C. Aliphatic-magnitude values on a methyl-carbon and an aromatic-carbon name: an atom-naming or assignment mismatch, not a units error. Nothing to recover from the record.
CG2 at 43.5-50.6 ppm against a corpus range of 13.1-25.8, Atom_type=C, Val_err 0.40. Same class as BMRB 26552.

22 nitrogens at 206.3-224.5 ppm against a corpus range of 101.9-137.3, Atom_type=N, no Val_err. Far outside amide nitrogen and not a transposition. Cause not established -- a different referencing standard and a non-amide nitrogen are both consistent with what the record shows.

Five Arg NE all at exactly 149.11 ppm against a corpus range of 77.6-130.2. Arg NE sits near 84.6 ppm and is known to alias by roughly one 15N sweep width; 149.11 is about two widths off, so folding is plausible but unproven. Treat as unusable rather than as a structural observation.

Five HD23 at 3.75-4.10 ppm against a corpus 99.9th percentile of 3.56 -- barely outside, on five cells. Most likely a genuine downfield methyl and a false positive of the range test; recorded so it is not rediscovered as new.
